a: git rebase -i lets you squash, reorder, and edit commits cleanly.
Cherry-pick applies a specific commit onto another branch.
Bisect binary-searches history to find the commit that introduced a bug.
Worktrees check out multiple branches in parallel directories.
Reflog records where HEAD pointed; useful to recover lost commits.
Sparse checkout checks out only part of a large monorepo.
Signed commits prove authorship with GPG/SSH signatures.
Trunk-based dev uses short-lived branches and frequent integration to main.
Server-side hooks enforce policy on push (tests, message format).
